discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived and championed the idea of turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope, and led IceCube from concept through construction to discovery. In 2013 IceCube reported the first evidence for a diffuse flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, with PeV-energy events far above the atmospheric background, later confirmed at high significance. This opened an entirely new observational window on the universe: neutrinos, unaffected by magnetic fields and matter, point back to the most violent cosmic accelerators. Subsequent results, including the 2017 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the 2023 observation of neutrinos from the Galactic plane, established neutrino astronomy as a working discipline and a pillar of multi-messenger astrophysics. The idea was simple; realising it at the South Pole was a technical triumph of the highest order. This is a clearly defined discovery, not an incremental improvement.
